item.description: The current implementation of _normalize_path_segments function (lines 134-157) does not correctly handle path normalization according to RFC 3986, particularly when dealing with ".." segments that would go above the root of the path.
item.contract: The function must properly implement RFC 3986 path normalization rules for ".." segments. When processing a path like "μονοπάτι/../../να/𝕦𝕟𝕚/𝕔𝕠𝕕𝕖/.", the result should be "/να/𝕦𝕟𝕚/𝕔𝕠𝕕𝕖/" not "/../να/𝕦𝕟𝕚/𝕔𝕠𝕕𝕖". The function should properly handle cases where ".." segments would go beyond the root of the path.
item.acceptance: Test case test_join_path_normalized with input "μονοπάτι/../../να/𝕦𝕟𝕚/𝕔𝕠𝕕𝕖/." should pass, expecting result "/να/𝕦𝕟𝕚/𝕔𝕠𝕕𝕖/"

item.description: The with_path method (line 1252) incorrectly applies path normalization only when "." is present in the path, but it should normalize all paths that contain "." or ".." segments according to RFC 3986.
item.contract: The with_path method should normalize paths consistently when they contain "." or ".." segments, regardless of whether they are at the beginning or middle of the path. For example, with_path("/test/.") should return "/test/" not "/test".
item.acceptance: Test case test_with_path_dots should pass, verifying that str(url.with_path("/test/.")) equals "http://example.com/test/"

item.description: The _normalize_path function (line 996) does not correctly handle the case where a path starts with "./" or "../" segments that need to be normalized.
item.contract: The _normalize_path function should correctly process paths that begin with "./" or "../" segments, ensuring they are normalized according to RFC 3986 rules. The function should handle absolute paths correctly while preserving the root slash.
item.acceptance: Test cases involving path normalization with leading dots should pass, such as joining path "../path/to" or "./path/to"
